assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single-molecule electrical readout of polymers through a pore is a clean physical principle (ionic current blockade, quantitative and single-molecule resolution) that became a real capability: portable long-read DNA/RNA sequencing and a generic platform for single-molecule analytics. It opens unforeseen opportunities, which I value.
assessment.attribution: Deamer, Branton and Kasianowicz-era proof of concept, Bayley's engineered protein pores (chemistry-driven design), and Akeson's enzyme-controlled translocation are the decisive steps. Three-way split is plausible but excludes Branton and Kasianowicz; I would want the committee to test who did what and when.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed and in routine use for over a decade across many labs; recognition is timely, with the core discovery well separated from later commercial refinements.
uncertainties: Whether the chemistry content (engineered pores, motor-controlled translocation) is judged sufficient for a chemistry prize rather than physics/medicine.
Credit allocation among Deamer, Branton, Kasianowicz, Bayley and Akeson is contested; I am relying on general knowledge rather than verified primary history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle in cells is a physical-chemistry concept with quantitative thermodynamic underpinnings and wide generative potential across cell biology and disease. It reframes how compartmentalization without membranes works.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne's P-granule work is the originating observation; Rosen's multivalent-interaction phase-diagram work gave the quantitative framework. Pappu and Mittag contributed sequence-encoded physics. A three-person configuration is defensible but leaves out important theorists.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation of the phenomenon, but debate persists on the physiological relevance and the definition of condensates in vivo; maturity is moderate to good and the field is still evolving quickly.
uncertainties: Disputes over how many reported cellular condensates are truly liquid-like phase separation.
Whether this is chemistry or better placed in physiology/medicine.
Unresolved credit between experimental and theoretical contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity through bifunctional degraders and molecular glues is a new mode of drug action that makes previously undruggable targets accessible, with clinical-stage drugs. A strong example of a conceptual chemical invention that opens vast possibilities.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept; Ciulli delivered structure-guided, potent VHL-based degraders; Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, a separate and compelling part of the story. Compound discovery with real credit allocation problems.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is accumulating but approvals are still limited; recognition may be slightly early, though mechanistic evidence is robust.
uncertainties: Clinical outcomes still maturing.
Whether molecular glue and PROTAC strands should be recognized together.
Many credited names; fair configuration is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Resolving the bond-level structure of individual molecules with a CO-functionalized tip is a physical-instrumentation achievement approaching atomic resolution. It turns the structural formula into a direct image and enables on-surface chemistry studies. Conceptually clear and striking.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl (qPlus sensor), Gross and Meyer (CO-tip imaging, 2009) are the decisive contributors; Eigler and Ho are earlier STM pioneers whose manipulation work is a distinct earlier thread. The three-person subset is coherent.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced in many labs for over a decade; mature. Applications are specialized rather than broad, which tempers the impact.
uncertainties: Breadth of impact in chemistry beyond specialist surface science.
STM/AFM prior recognition (1986 physics) may be seen as overlapping.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another without double-strand cleavage, a chemically designed deaminase-fusion approach with major therapeutic and research significance, and clinical use has begun.
assessment.attribution: Liu's lab made the decisive contribution; Komor and Gaudelli were lead authors of the cytosine and adenine editors. Nishida and Kondo reported a related deaminase approach. Liu is clearly central.
assessment.maturity: Widely confirmed and in clinical trials, but the 2020 prize for CRISPR may make the committee wary of recognizing a follow-on technology so soon.
uncertainties: Overlap with prime editing as a competing or joint citation.
Distance from the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Whether the contribution is regarded as chemistry rather than molecular biology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Unifying electronic-structure and molecular dynamics so atoms move under quantum forces is a fundamental methodological advance that underlies much of modern simulation of liquids, interfaces and materials. A clean principle with huge reach.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 Car-Parrinello paper is a well-defined two-person contribution, a natural pair. Credit is unambiguous.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of validation; very mature, arguably overdue, but the 2013 and 2024 computational prizes could reduce urgency.
uncertainties: Competition from other computational candidates for a limited number of slots.
Whether the committee views DFT-related methods as already honored.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites reached high solar-cell efficiency with remarkable speed, a materials-chemistry discovery of broad energy relevance. From a physicist's view the scientific principle (defect tolerance, long carrier lifetimes) is interesting but not yet fully settled.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first used perovskites as sensitizers; Park, Grätzel and Snaith made the efficiency and solid-state breakthroughs. Seok and Park contributed to the efficiency race. Many comparable contributors make a fair three-person split hard.
assessment.maturity: Fast progress but stability and scale-up remain unresolved; possibly premature for a prize.
uncertainties: Long-term stability and commercialization are unproven.
Contested credit among Miyasaka, Park, Snaith, Grätzel and Seok.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective C-H functionalization changes how molecules can be built and is deeply influential in synthesis and pharmaceutical chemistry, though I judge it mainly through specialist input from other members.
assessment.attribution: Yu (directing groups and ligands), Hartwig (borylation and amination) and Sanford (Pd-catalyzed functionalization) are leaders; Bergman and Daugulis are important originators. Attribution is crowded and unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely used; progress is incremental across many groups and the original discovery is difficult to isolate.
uncertainties: Hard to isolate a single discovery from many parallel advances.
Overlap with prior catalysis prizes.
I defer to synthetic chemists on technical depth.
